_readme: Hand-maintained. The build script reads this file and never rewrites it.
The SEC's ticker map is regenerated daily from filing cover pages, so when a company
reorganises, a ticker can move to a freshly registered holding CIK that has filed
nothing yet — leaving the operating company, with all the history, carrying no ticker.
A reader resolving the ticker then joins to a CIK with no fundamentals at all.
Each entry forces one ticker to one CIK. It is applied where data/tickers.json is built,
so it flows through to every company file's `tickers`, to the manifest, and to
data/sp500.json; build_sec_events.py reads the same file so the operating company's
8-Ks are tagged with the ticker too.
Add an entry only when the SEC map points a ticker at a shell with no filings, and say
why. Remove it once the SEC map catches up — check before assuming an entry is still
needed. `name` is optional and only cosmetic (data/tickers.json); the authoritative name
is the entityName in the company's own file.

XOM.name: Exxon Mobil Corporation
XOM.why: The SEC map points XOM at CIK 2115436 (ExxonMobil Holdings Corp), a new registrant with no companyfacts history. All the fundamentals — 8 fiscal years to FY2025, revenue $332bn — are filed under CIK 34088, which the map left with no ticker.
